newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. body refers parking row to General Assembly.
newsitem.headline: U.N. body refers parking row to General Assembly.

text.p: After a month-long campaign against new regulations denying diplomats exemption from paying New York city parking fines, a U.N. committee on Thursday referrd the issue to the 185-nation General Assembly.
The vote in the 15-member committee on relations with the host country was 13 in favour, with only the United States opposed and Britain abstaining.
Under the new regulations, unveiled on March 10 and put into effect on April 1, diplomats failing to clear up their parking fines within 12 months would lose their special parking plates.
Each country is also guaranteed two parking spaces outside its U.N. mission and one outside the residence of its ambassador, though these provisions have yet to be fully applied.

The U.N. legal counsel has ruled that parts of the programme violate international law on diplomatic immunity and privileges. The issue has also become a source of friction in the uneasy relationship between the United Nations, its host city and some New Yorkers, angered over what they regard as diplomatic "scofflaws" who until now have been able to escape paying parking fines.

Many speakers said they would agree not to turn the matter over to the General Assembly if the United States promised the disputed provisions would be suspended while negotiations continued for a few more days in a bid to resolve differences.
The United States promised to be flexible, but this failed to satisfy most members and the issue was pressed to a vote, even though the committee usually acts by consensus.
